rows.why: Item 12 asks what the default share is. It picks 7500 bps, and the run shows a bounty of 1000 releasing 750 with no share configured. A bounty of 10000 would release 7500, and item 7's run shows the status is 'partially released' after a pass.

Item 1 asks how the share is rounded. It rounds down using BigInt integer division and gives the remainder to UAT. The run returns 101 → 33 + 68, which adds up to the bounty. BigInt keeps the result exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so 999 would give 749 + 250.

Item 8 asks what UAT approval releases. It releases the bounty minus what has already been released, and the status becomes 'fully released'. The run shows 10 already released, then 90 more, with status 'fully released'.

Item 9 asks what a failed run records. It returns the current state, or a fresh 'locked' state, without saving. The run returns { status: 'locked', releases: [] }. The one save in that run comes from the pass that follows the failure.
Item 6 asks about UAT approval before the hidden tests pass. It throws 'cannot approve UAT: the hidden tests have not passed', with 0 saves and the state still undefined.
Item 5 asks what a zero bounty does. The status is 'pro bono', but on a pass it still records a hidden-tests release of amount 0. The scenario says no release is ever recorded.

Item 7 asks how a repeated event is treated. It checks the stored release kinds and ignores the event id, so both the same event again and a different hidden-tests-passed event record nothing. The run shows the second event, with a different id, causing no new save.

Item 10 asks about concurrent events. They all go through one promise queue, so the dedup by release kind from item 7 applies to each in turn. The run uses a delayed store and sends two hidden-tests-passed at once (same id), and only one hidden-tests release appears. Different ids and two concurrent uat-approved weren't run, but the same queue and kind check would cover them.
Item 11 asks what happens when the store fails. The event rejects with the store's error and nothing is recorded. The run shows 'store down', and retrying the same event then succeeds.
